summary: Revised CL-100 cab on a 14-ft block tower in Siskiyou County, built 1978 to replace a 1934 CCC lookout; the register says it is actively staffed.

facts.design: Revised CL-100 cabin design on a 14-ft block tower
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Earlier lookout, an L-4 cab on an enclosed timber tower, constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps
John Thomas of Happy Camp returned as lookout at Ukonom (first named lookout in the sources read)
Ida Lake employed as lookout in the Ukonom District
A 1963 item says Ida Lake had worked the post for a number of years and spent a fire season there
Forest Service introduced a lookout-at-home post; Edith Crawford served from her summer home
Current structure: revised CL-100 cabin design on a 14-ft block tower; cab moved from the Lower Devils lookout
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register lists the Klamath National Forest as administrator and says the Six Rivers National Forest actively staffs and manages the lookout.

notes_for_editor: Staffing 'staffed' as_of 2019 is the register's undated present-tense text, taken with its 2019 registration date; no current staffing schedule was found. The Forest Service district page I checked had no lookout listing. The 14-ft tower height is converted to 4.3 m. Access left out of facts: the sources read give no current visiting rules (the only visiting statement is from 1971). The 1934 CCC date is from the register; the Forest Lookouts page repeats it from a Klamath NF history volume that I did not read directly. Record fields other than these were not checked. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1951, 1961, 1963 and 1971 dates were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page and added to the evidence quotes; the story now says 'an earlier lookout' because the register says 'earlier', not 'first'.
